title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
summary: Given a directed acyclic graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and edges defined by an array, identify the minimum set of nodes from which all other nodes are reachable.
statement: Given a directed acyclic graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and edges defined by an array, identify the minimum set of nodes from which all other nodes are reachable. Ensure the solution is unique and can be presented in any order.
constraints: Nodes are zero through n-1 and edges form a DAG.
Return the unique minimum set of starting nodes from which every node is reachable; order does not matter.
reference_solution:
def minimum_start_vertices(n, edges):
 incoming=[False]*n
 for source,target in edges:incoming[target]=True
 return [node for node in range(n) if not incoming[node]]

hints: Every indegree-zero node is unreachable from any other node, so each must be selected.
Every positive-indegree node has a predecessor.
Following predecessors in a finite DAG eventually reaches an indegree-zero source.
Therefore exactly the indegree-zero nodes are necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: Only nodes zero and three have no incoming edge, so both are necessary and together reach all nodes.
Zero, two, and three have indegree zero and form the minimum source set.
